short: The actual movement of money in and out of the business.
seoTitle: Cash Flow — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Cash flow is the movement of money into and out of a business over a period. Businesses fail from running out of cash, not from making losses on paper.
definition: Cash flow is the movement of money into and out of a business over a period. Positive cash flow means more came in than went out — a different question entirely from whether the business was profitable.
bodyHtml:
Why Cash Flow matters

Businesses fail from running out of cash, not from making losses on paper. Profit pays the owner eventually; cash pays the salaries this Friday.

Cash Flow formula

Net cash flow = Cash inflows − Cash outflows for the period

Operating cash flow excludes loans and capital spending.

How Cash Flow works in practice

Forecast weekly for the next quarter, listing expected collections and committed payments. Even a rough forecast surfaces the tight week early enough to do something about it.

faq.question: Why is my business profitable but short of cash?
faq.answer: Stock, unpaid invoices, loan repayments and owner drawings all consume cash without reducing profit.

faq.question: How far ahead should I forecast?
faq.answer: Thirteen weeks is the standard working horizon — long enough to act, short enough to be credible.
